question: us-policy-positions:environment-energy.ban-new-gas-hookups
definition: yes = a state law in force on 2026-01-01 bars gas hookups in new buildings statewide; no = the state preempts local governments from banning or restricting gas connections by fuel type; everything else is unknown (local-allowed or not-found).
summarySource: E&E News 'Capital control' and S&P Global trackers (2023-2025: 24-26 preemption states, ME 2025, ND/SD 2023); Spectrum/Canary Media (Nov 2025 NY delay); Ballotpedia and Washington State Standard (I-2066, 2025-2026). Web-search budget ran out after 4 queries, so most states are unverified.

US-ME.note: Maine enacted a 2025 'energy choice' law preempting local gas bans; the statute cite and effective date were not confirmed in search results.

US-ND.note: North Dakota enacted an energy-choice preemption law in March 2023 (reported as the 22nd or 23rd state); cite and exact effective date not confirmed.

US-SD.note: South Dakota enacted an energy-choice preemption law in March 2023 (reported as the 22nd or 23rd state); cite and exact effective date not confirmed.

conflicts.readings: Statute bars gas hookups in new low-rise buildings from 2026-01-01 (yes) vs. implementation delayed by court-filed agreement pending Second Circuit ruling, so not in force on 2026-01-01 (no statewide ban).
I-2066 preempts local gas restrictions from 2024-12-05 (no) vs. held unconstitutional by trial court 2025-03-21 and by the state Supreme Court 2026-09-17 (local-allowed).
